items.title: Tale of two private jets
items.description: This is a tale of two private jets, bought for two chief ministers, on two different continents, in two different worlds. While a debate rages in Pakistan about the purchase and use of a private jet by Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz, the Premier (chief minister) of Ontario, the largest province of Canada with a GDP of roughly C$900.8 billion (US $643.54bn) in 2017 terms, also had to face a similar outcry when the provincial government announced on April 17 this year, the purchase of a Canada made, ten years old, 2016 model, pre-owned Bombardier Challenger 650 jet for Premier Doug Ford’s “extensive travel(s)”. The jet, bought for C$28.9 million, was to facilitate the Premier’s travel within Ontario and the United States, the announcement said. Announcing the purchase, a spokesperson for the Ontario government then said that the plane would be used solely to conduct “government business”, and not for any personal trip. Premier Ford argued then that the province needed the plane because Ontario is vast, and he needed something more secure to travel to the United States to push back against President Donald Trump’s trade war . Compared to what happened in Pakistan, when the premier of Canada’s Ontario faced backlash over the purchase of a plane, he reversed his decision While defending the purchase, Mr Ford’s office also cited that the plane was necessary for “more certain, flexible, secure and confidential travel,” citing the premier’s trips across the province as well as to meetings with fellow premiers and the prime minister. The purchase resulted in an uproar. Critics quickly derided it as the “gravy plane” — a play on Ford’s boasts in the past that he was elected to “stop the gravy train” of government spending. All guns targeted Premier Doug Ford for the purchase. Ontario Opposition Leader Marit Stiles, of the New Democratic Party (NDP), called the jet a “gravy plane” in a social media post, adding that Ford should be “flying economy like the rest of us.” Premier Doug Ford faced an outcry when the provincial government announced the purchase of a Canada-made, ten-year-old, pre-owned jet for C$28.9 million “I think it’s outrageous that the premier would be considering spending 30 million [Canadian] dollars on a luxury private plane at a time like this — when Ontarians are struggling with the price of rent, the price of food,” Stiles said at an unrelated news conference then. The NDP, in its statement, also cited a 2019 Toronto Star story , in which Ford had said that he was “the only premier in history” who would prefer to drive around the province than spend taxpayer dollars flying. Interim Ontario Liberal Leader John Fraser strongly condemned the Ford government’s purchase of the pre-owned Bombardier Challenger 650 private jet, calling it completely “out of touch”. Groups outside of the opposition benches were also quick to denounce the provincial government’s purchase. The Canadian Taxpayers Federation (CTF) demanded in a statement that Ford reverse plans to spend taxpayer dollars on a private jet. “Instead of taking commercial flights like many premiers in this country do, Ford would rather cosplay the life of the rich and famous on taxpayers’ dime,” said Noah Jarvis, CTF Ontario director. “Ordinary taxpayers are struggling to make ends meet, and (Ontario premier) Ford is making them pay for a personal jet so that he doesn’t have to wait in line at the airport like everyone else.” And with public pressure piling on the purchases, both in Pakistan and in Canada, the outcomes of the two were starkly opposite to each other. Here in Toronto, the outcry forced Premier Ford to change his decision. He had to take a U-turn. Within a few days of the announcement of the jet purchase, Mr Ford gave in, conceding that he had heard the public’s concerns. “Despite the best of intentions, I have heard and agree that now is not the right time for the expense of a government plane. The province is working with Bombardier and other partners to sell the plane as quickly as possible,” he said. Speaking at an unrelated announcement in Ottawa, he then added, “I’m the premier that listens to the people, and if they don’t like something, I’m not too shy to change my mind”. Within days, the plane was sold back to Bombardier at the purchase price of C$28.9 million. But Premier Ford is not out of the woods. The purchase, and the expenses involved in the process, cost the provincial exchequer an additional amount of around C$200,000. He will have to answer that too. Premier Doug Ford is known as a go-getter. He has won three consecutive elections in the province for the provincial Conservatives. Yet, pundits now believe his party may have to pay a political price for the decision to buy a private jet for the premier of Canada’s largest province, which boasts the highest GDP among the provinces of the country. Real democracy is at work — at least here in Canada. The writer is a Canadian-based analyst. X: @rhusainsyed Published in Dawn, The Business and Finance Weekly, September 28th, 2026

items.title: NPP demands review of GH¢2,650 cocoa price, questions statutory calculation
items.description: The New Patriotic Party (NPP) has called for a review of the government’s GH¢2,650 producer price for a 64-kilogramme bag of cocoa for the 2026/27 season, arguing that the figure is inadequate and does not meet the statutory requirement under the new cocoa law. In a statement dated September 27, the opposition party questioned the basis on which the government arrived at the new price, particularly its calculation of the percentage of the Gross Free-on-Board (FOB) value being paid to cocoa farmers. The government, through the Ghana Cocoa Board (COCOBOD), announced the new producer price on September 25, increasing it from GH¢2,587 per 64kg bag in the previous season to GH¢2,650. The increase amounts to GH¢63 per bag, or about 2.4 per cent. COCOBOD says the new price of GH¢42,400 per tonne, equivalent to GH¢2,650 per bag, represents 71.18 per cent of the realised gross FOB value of cocoa. The announcement was made under the Ghana Cocoa Board Act, 2026 (Act 1182), which provides for a minimum of 70 per cent of the realised gross FOB price to be paid to cocoa farmers. However, the NPP disputes the government’s calculation and says the figures underpinning the 71.18 per cent claim require greater transparency. The party has therefore challenged the government to review the producer price to ensure what it considers full compliance with the statutory provision. NPP raises campaign promise Beyond the statutory argument, the NPP also accused the governing National Democratic Congress (NDC) of failing to fulfil promises it made to cocoa farmers during the 2024 election campaign. According to the opposition party, leading NDC figures, including President John Dramani Mahama, Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson, Food and Agriculture Minister Eric Opoku and Health Minister Kwabena Mintah Akandoh, engaged cocoa-growing communities during the campaign and promised a producer price of GH¢6,000 per bag. The NPP said farmers were also told that the GH¢3,100 per bag then being paid was exploitative and that cocoa farmers deserved at least 70 per cent of the international market price. The party argues that the GH¢2,650 announced for the 2026/27 season falls substantially below that campaign figure. Government’s position The government’s announced price, however, is presented by COCOBOD as being above the 70 per cent threshold contained in Act 1182. COCOBOD said the new price followed consultations involving the Ministry of Finance, cocoa farmers and other stakeholders in the cocoa value chain, including licensed buying companies, hauliers and processors. The new pricing forms part of broader reforms introduced under the 2026 Act, including changes intended to strengthen the financial sustainability and governance of the cocoa sector and improve returns to farmers. The dispute now centres on whether the GH¢2,650 price accurately reflects the statutory 70 per cent minimum and whether the government’s calculation of the realised gross FOB value provides sufficient basis for the announced figure.

items.title: AFCON 2027Q: ‘Better to stay home if you’re coming to complain about absent players’ – Carlos Queiroz
items.description: Black Stars head coach Carlos Queiroz has urged Ghanaian supporters to back the players available for Tuesday’s 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifier against The Gambia rather than focus on those missing from the squad. Ghana are looking to recover from their 2-0 defeat to Côte d’Ivoire in Bouaké in their opening Group C fixture. The defeat has increased the pressure on the Black Stars to respond in front of their home supporters at the Accra Sports Stadium. With several key players unavailable, Queiroz says fans who come to the stadium must be prepared to support those selected to represent Ghana. “It’s better to stay home if you’re coming to the stadium to complain about players that are not here instead of supporting those that are here,” Queiroz said. The Black Stars have had to deal with several absences ahead of the qualifiers, with Mohammed Kudus, Antoine Semenyo and Nathaniel Adjei among the players unavailable. A number of replacements have since been brought into the squad as Queiroz prepares for his first competitive home game since returning for a second spell as Ghana coach. The Portuguese coach is hoping the support from the stands will help his team respond to the defeat in Bouaké and get their qualification campaign back on track. For Ghana, Tuesday’s fixture offers an opportunity to claim their first points in Group C and restore some confidence after a disappointing opening result. The Black Stars host The Gambia at the Accra Sports Stadium as they begin the fight to return to the Africa Cup of Nations after missing the 2025 tournament.

items.title: Investors who relocated from Abia should return — Otti
items.description: ABIA — Abia State Governor, Alex Otti, has called on investors who previously relocated from the state to return and take advantage of what he described as the growing investment opportunities in the state. Otti made the call on Monday while announcing the commissioning of the 55-room ORIS Signature Hotel on Okigwe Road, Aba. The governor, in a post on his X platform, commended the Chief Executive Officer of the hotel, Owelle Greg Okafor, for completing the project within two years and a few months. He described the hotel as a significant addition to Aba’s hospitality and investment landscape, saying its completion demonstrated what could be achieved when vision, enterprise and a conducive business environment came together. According to him, Aba faced significant challenges when his administration assumed office, including poor road infrastructure and struggling industries. He said the situation was gradually changing, with businesses returning, property values rising and new investments taking shape. Otti therefore invited investors who had previously relocated from Abia, as well as prospective investors, to return and take advantage of the opportunities being created by his administration. “What we have achieved so far is only the beginning,” the governor said, adding that the completion of more projects would further strengthen Aba’s position as an economic hub. He specifically mentioned the soon-to-be-completed Radisson Blu Enyimba Hotel as one of the projects expected to contribute to the city’s continued growth. Otti also acknowledged guests, friends and well-wishers who attended the commissioning and supported what he described as the growth and transformation of Aba and Abia State. He congratulated Okafor and the entire ORIS Signature Hotel team on the completion of the project. “Together, we will continue to build an Abia where businesses and investments can thrive and opportunities abound,” the governor said. The post Investors who relocated from Abia should return — Otti appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Santé de la reproduction : les jeunes prennent la parole
items.description: Le Réseau des jeunes ambassadeurs pour la promotion de la santé de la reproduction et de la planification familiale (JASRPF), en collaboration avec l’ONG RAES, a conduit des activités de mobilisation des adolescents et des jeunes dans le cadre de la campagne « C’est la vie ! » au Burkina Faso. Au cours de la période 2025-2026, les actions menées ont notamment porté sur la création de clubs scolaires et l’organisation d’une activité artistique ayant mobilisé plus d’une centaine de jeunes à Bobo-Dioulasso. La connaissance du corps, la planification familiale et la prévention des pratiques néfastes figurent parmi les thèmes abordés par le Réseau des jeunes ambassadeurs pour la promotion de la santé de la reproduction et de la planification familiale (JASRPF) lors de ses activités de sensibilisation au profit de leurs pairs. En s’appuyant sur des approches participatives et ludiques, les interventions du JASRPF ont permis aux jeunes de s’approprier les messages clés, d’exprimer leurs perceptions et leurs expériences et de développer une meilleure compréhension de leurs droits et responsabilités. Sensibiliser les adolescents et les jeunes aux droits et à la santé sexuels et reproductifs ne consiste plus seulement à leur transmettre des informations. Avec « C’est la vie ! – Phase II », du Réseau africain pour la santé et l’éducation (RAES), l’enjeu a également été de leur donner une place active dans le processus de sensibilisation. En effet, à Ouagadougou et à Bobo-Dioulasso, les jeunes ambassadeurs et les pairs éducateurs du JASRPF/BF ont animé plusieurs activités autour de la santé sexuelle et reproductive, de la planification familiale, des grossesses précoces et non désirées, des infections sexuellement transmissibles, des violences basées sur le genre, ainsi que des mariages et unions précoces. Au cours de la période, huit causeries éducatives ont permis de toucher directement 80 adolescents et jeunes, dont 51 garçons et 29 filles. Les échanges, basés sur le dialogue et les questions-réponses, ont notamment utilisé le kit éducatif « C’est la vie ! ». Pour le président du JASRPF/BF, Arthur Daboné, au-delà du nombre de participants, l’intérêt de cette démarche réside dans le rôle confié aux jeunes. Ceux-ci ne sont pas seulement bénéficiaires des messages : ils deviennent progressivement des relais capables d’échanger avec leurs pairs et de contribuer à la diffusion de l’information dans leurs milieux de vie. Des réalisations satisfaisantes Les activités destinées aux leaders religieux et communautaires ont réuni 46 participants, contre une cible de 40. Avec ces personnes-ressources, les discussions ont notamment porté sur les normes sociales et les conséquences des mariages et unions précoces. Les participants ont été invités à contribuer à la diffusion des messages de prévention au sein de leurs communautés. Les quatre ciné-débats organisés à Ouagadougou et à Bobo-Dioulasso ont, pour leur part, rassemblé 260 adolescents et jeunes, alors que la cible était d’au moins 200 participants. La projection des épisodes de « C’est la vie ! » a servi de point de départ aux échanges. Les jeunes ont ensuite pu réagir, poser leurs questions et discuter avec les pairs éducateurs et des professionnels de santé. Cette formule, soutient Alima Coulibaly, animatrice du réseau des JASRPF mêlant audiovisuel, discussion et intervention de professionnels, semble avoir facilité la prise de parole des jeunes sur des questions parfois difficiles à aborder dans les cadres traditionnels de sensibilisation. Le projet a également choisi de sortir des cadres classiques de la sensibilisation en associant messages de santé et activités sportives. Deux tournois mixtes de football et de handball, organisés à Ouagadougou et à Bobo-Dioulasso, ont mobilisé environ 644 adolescents et jeunes, participants et spectateurs confondus. La particularité de ces rencontres résidait dans la constitution d’équipes mixtes et dans l’intégration de séquences éducatives entre les matchs. Les participants ont notamment été sensibilisés au fonctionnement du corps, à l’égalité entre les sexes et aux questions liées à la santé sexuelle et reproductive. Si les activités communautaires ont permis des échanges directs, la radio a donné au projet une capacité de diffusion beaucoup plus importante. Quatre émissions interactives ont été réalisées au cours de la période. Elles ont permis de toucher environ 100 000 auditeurs cumulés. Les jeunes ambassadeurs et les points focaux ont participé à la préparation et à l’animation des émissions, donnant ainsi une place centrale à la parole des jeunes. I nscrire les acquis dans la durée L’une des avancées importantes du projet est la création de huit clubs de santé sexuelle et reproductive des adolescents et des jeunes dans des établissements scolaires de Ouagadougou et de Bobo-Dioulasso. Environ 80 jeunes y sont activement impliqués, avec une attention portée à la parité. Ces clubs constituent une évolution importante dans la stratégie d’intervention. Contrairement aux activités ponctuelles, ils peuvent servir de relais permanents pour l’information et l’éducation par les pairs. Selon Béatrice OUEDRAOGO, chargée de communication du réseau des JASRPF. Ils offrent également aux adolescent.e.s et jeunes un espace où ils peuvent échanger, poser des questions, partager des informations et contribuer eux-mêmes à la sensibilisation de leurs camarades. Pour le projet, cette dynamique favorise l’appropriation des messages et contribue à faire émerger de jeunes leaders capables de poursuivre les actions au sein de leurs établissements. Le défi sera désormais de consolider les clubs scolaires, de maintenir l’engagement des jeunes ambassadeurs et de renforcer les passerelles entre information, dialogue et accès à des services de santé adaptés aux adolescents et aux jeunes retorque SANOU Leonel membre dudit réseau. Boureima SANGA

items.title: Trump a proposé à Xi Jinping d’acheter des armes américaines
items.description: Donald Trump a demande a Xi Jinping si la Chine souhaitait acheter des armes americaines, selon l'ambassadeur des etats-Unis a Pekin David Perdue, qui s'exprimait dimanche 27 septembre. Washington a toutefois rapidement assure qu'aucune vente n'etait reellement envisagee. Interroge sur Fox News a propos des livraisons d'armes a Taïwan, le diplomate a explique que Trump avait rappele a son homologue chinois que les etats-Unis vendaient du materiel militaire « a d'autres pays dans le monde », avant de lui demander, « a un moment donne », s'il souhaitait lui aussi en acheter. L'ambassadeur n'a precise ni la date de cet echange, ni la reaction de Xi. Un enieme bluff de Trump Le departement d'etat a immediatement tempere ces propos : la legislation americaine interdit les ventes d'armes a la Chine et il n'existe « aucune offre ni aucun projet » en ce sens. L'episode survient dans un contexte sensible autour de Taïwan. Pekin considere l'île comme faisant partie de son territoire et demande regulierement a Washington de cesser de l'armer. Les etats-Unis restent le principal fournisseur militaire de Taipei. Une vente record de 11 milliards de dollars avait ete approuvee en decembre 2025, tandis qu'un nouveau paquet d'environ 14 milliards est bloque depuis plusieurs mois. Trump avait lui-meme qualifie ce dossier de « tres bon levier de negociation » face a Pekin. Lors de la visite de Xi a Washington le 24 septembre, le dirigeant chinois a de nouveau demande aux etats-Unis de s'opposer a l'independance de Taïwan. La sortie de l'ambassadeur ne signifie donc pas qu'un contrat sino-americain soit en preparation. Elle coïncide avec une periode ou l'administration Trump cherche a stabiliser ses relations avec Pekin tout en negociant sur Taïwan, le commerce et les questions strategiques. Une veritable livraison d'armes americaines a la Chine constituerait, elle, une rupture majeure avec plusieurs decennies de politique americaine.

items.title: First Deputy Minority Whip files private members’ motion for inquiry into Ghana-linked narcotics seizures
items.description: The First Deputy Minority Whip and Member of Parliament for Tolon, Habib Iddrisu, has filed a private members’ motion seeking a parliamentary inquiry into a series of high-profile narcotics seizures linked to Ghana. The motion, dated September 28, 2026, and submitted to the Clerk to Parliament under Standing Order 102, is co-sponsored by eight other New Patriotic Party (NPP) MPs. They are Rev. John Ntim Fordjour, Osahen Alexander Afenyo-Markin, Kojo Oppong Nkrumah, Dominic Nitiwul, Abena Osei-Asare, Patrick Boamah, Alhassan Tampuli, Mahama Abdul Kabiru and Samuel Awuku. The proposed inquiry comes ahead of Parliament’s extraordinary sitting on Tuesday, September 29, which was summoned by Speaker Alban Bagbin following a petition led by Mr Iddrisu over recent narcotics seizures linked to Ghana. The motion seeks the establishment of an Ad Hoc Committee under Article 103 of the 1992 Constitution and Order 262 of Parliament’s Standing Orders to conduct what the sponsors describe as a thorough, transparent and bipartisan inquiry. The committee would examine the circumstances surrounding a number of major narcotics seizures, including the nearly 3.9 metric tonnes of cocaine seized by French Customs at Dunkirk on September 10. The motion puts the value of that consignment at about US$261 million. French authorities have separately reported the seizure at an estimated €225 million. It also cites the 320kg methamphetamine seizure in Australia in June 2026, as well as major cocaine interceptions in Ghana in 2025. The sponsors are further asking the committee to examine any other narcotics-related seizure linked to Ghana since the beginning of the Ninth Parliament. A key part of the proposed inquiry would be an examination of how the consignments were processed, inspected, cleared and exported from Ghana. The committee would investigate the ports of departure and the security procedures applied, including intelligence profiling, scanning, physical inspection and customs clearance. It would also seek to establish the identities and roles of companies, state agencies and other entities involved in processing and clearing the consignments, subject to restrictions arising from ongoing criminal investigations. The motion further proposes an assessment of the adequacy of scanning, surveillance, intelligence and other security systems at Ghana’s seaports, airports and points of entry and exit. The proposed committee would also examine the status of investigations, arrests and prosecutions arising from the various seizures. It would assess the level of cooperation and intelligence sharing between Ghanaian authorities and their counterparts in France, Australia and other jurisdictions. Another area of focus would be efforts to identify the alleged financiers, organisers, facilitators and wider networks behind major narcotics trafficking operations. The committee would subsequently recommend legislative, administrative, security and institutional reforms aimed at preventing Ghana from being used as an origin, transit or operational point for international narcotics trafficking. The motion comes after the Minority Caucus petitioned the Speaker for an extraordinary sitting over what it described as urgent national security concerns arising from the seizures. Speaker Bagbin subsequently summoned Parliament to sit at noon on Tuesday, September 29, under Article 112(3) of the Constitution and the Standing Orders. The Speaker’s original notice did not specify the detailed business for the sitting. The Minority has argued that the scale of the seizures warrants parliamentary scrutiny, particularly regarding Ghana’s ports, customs controls, intelligence gathering and narcotics enforcement. The call for an inquiry has also received support from groups outside Parliament.

items.title: Heavy rain lashes twin cities as civic departments put on alert
items.description: RAWALPINDI: Islamabad and Rawalpindi received a fresh spell of rain on Monday, with civic departments in Rawalpindi placed on high alert on the commissioner’s orders. The Pakistan Meteorological Department (PMD) recorded 33mm of rain at Saidpur village on Monday morning. Golra, near E-11, received 25mm of rain, while Pirwadhai and Gawalmandi recorded 28mm and 27mm, respectively. According to PMD data, 23mm of rain was recorded in H-8, 22mm in I-12 and 29mm in Shamsabad. In its update, the PMD advised residents to stay away from Nullah Lai. “Nullah Lai is being continuously monitored, and the public is being kept informed in a timely manner,” Rawalpindi Commissioner Salman Ghani said. The water flow is currently normal, according to the authorities. The water level in Nullah Lai stands at 5.5 feet at Katarian and 2 feet at Gawalmandi. In a post on X, the Islamabad Traffic Police said its officers were ensuring a smooth flow of traffic and urged residents to adhere to traffic advisories and cooperate with the police. Heavy rain caused two flight diversions, Pakistan Airports Authority (PAA) said. A Pakistan International Airlines flight from Paris to Islamabad was diverted to Multan airport, where it landed at 5:44am, later departing for Islamabad at 8:21am, PAA said. Furthermore, an AirSial flight from Jeddah to Islamabad was diverted to Peshawar due to “bad weather”, landing at 10:25am, PAA said. Drainage operations were under way in the twin cities, while the Water and Sanitation Agency (Wasa) Rawalpindi had deployed staff and heavy machinery in low-lying areas. Heavy machinery had been stationed at Liaquat Bagh, Committee Chowk Underpass, Murree Road, Dhok Khabba, Circular Road and low-lying areas of Sadiqabad. Citizens were urged to contact the district administration or the Wasa helpline in case of an emergency. For the rest of the week, the PMD has forecast mainly dry weather in most parts of the country, while partly cloudy weather with isolated rain, wind and thunderstorms is expected in the northern hilly areas of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Gilgit-Baltistan. The National Disaster Management Authority has, meanwhile, released a report detailing casualties and damages recorded in rain-related incidents between June 26 and Sept 28. According to the report, 751 casualties, including 199 deaths, were recorded during this period from across the country. Among the deaths, 80 were reported from Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, 70 from Punjab, 19 from Sindh, seven from Azad Jammu and Kashmir and two from Islamabad. Moreover, 623 properties were fully damaged and 1,216 partially damaged in rain-related incidents across the country.

items.title: AON condemns airline picketing, warns of investor confidence loss
items.description: By Dickson Omobola Airline Operators of Nigeria, AON, has condemned what it described as the recent upsurge in the use of unions to threaten, harass and intimidate Nigerian airlines, saying such actions violate the rights of airlines to a safe, secure operational and business environment. AON, which lamented the recent picketing of Nigeria’s largest airline, Air Peace, said the carriers lost huge sums of revenue and incurred additional costs as a result of the disruptions. Rising from a meeting held at the Transcorp Hilton Hotel, Abuja, the airlines, in a communiqué, said Air Peace alone had more than 70 of its flights affected, with estimated losses of over N2 billion, while more than 30 flights operated by United Nigeria Airlines were affected, impacting about 13,000 passengers based on the aircraft and sectors scheduled for the day. They expressed sadness that the airlines had to bear the unwarranted burden of rebooking passengers, offering accommodation, paying refunds, repositioning crew, rescheduling aircraft and incurring other recovery costs in an already harsh operating environment characterised by unprecedentedly high fuel costs and very high foreign exchange-based maintenance costs. The communiqué reads: “On Tuesday, August 11, 2026, a group of Nigerian aviation unions and others outside the aviation industry embarked on a violent, disruptive action. “The disruptions occurred both at Murtala Muhammed Airport Terminal 1, MMA1, and Terminal 2, MMA2, as well as the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja, where the union members blocked access to Air Peace’s departure terminals. “The unions virtually brought all activities of the airline to a screeching halt by blocking the entrances to terminals and check-in counters and preventing airline workers from accessing their offices and workstations to check in passengers and offer services to passengers. “There were also recorded cases where members of these unions exhibited wilful acts of violence against airline staff and caused bodily harm to some of them. We consider these actions a flagrant violation of the fundamental rights of aviation workers going about their lawful duties and a serious threat to peace, safety and security within the airport environment. “The AON views these acts as a gross violation of the rights of airlines to a safe and secure operational and business environment and a shameful, despicable and very disturbing development with grave implications for the aviation industry in Nigeria. “ICAO Annex 17 defines ‘unlawful interference’ as ‘…acts or attempted acts such as to jeopardise the safety of civil aviation.’ From the foregoing, therefore, the unfortunate events of August 11, 2026, were effectively a violation of aviation safety and security regulations with serious immediate and future local and global implications for the aviation sector in Nigeria. “AON condemns very seriously the recent upsurge in the use of unions to threaten, harass and intimidate Nigerian airlines by certain quarters. It is illegal, unconstitutional and, above all, an aberration. Financial losses “Airlines lost huge sums of revenue, together with other additional costs, as a result of the disruptions. For instance, Air Peace alone had more than 70 of its flights affected, with estimated losses of over N2 billion. Similarly, more than 30 flights of United Nigeria Airlines were affected, impacting about 13,000 passengers, based on the aircraft and sectors scheduled for that day. “Furthermore, airlines had to carry the unwarranted burden of rebooking passengers, offering accommodation, paying refunds, repositioning crew, rescheduling aircraft and incurring other recovery costs in an already very harsh operating environment, with unprecedentedly high fuel costs, very high foreign exchange-based maintenance costs, etc. Disruption “Though the strike action took place mainly at the Lagos and Abuja airports, other flights across the entire domestic, regional and international networks of the airlines in the country were directly affected, as Lagos and Abuja are the domestic hubs that funnel capacity across the country’s entire airport system. Passengers were stranded throughout the nation and beyond. “Exposure of the vulnerability of airport infrastructure. It is instructive to put on record that the activities of the unions clearly undermined airport security regulations and exposed the vulnerability of Nigeria’s airport infrastructure, contrary to globally instituted provisions on aviation security. When the actions of unions result in passengers and airline staff being prevented from accessing airline terminals, the consequences extend beyond those involved. Investor confidence “No sooner did the activities of the unions begin to unfold on that fateful day than the confidence of investors in the Nigerian aviation sector began to wane. Lessors who had just recently begun to take interest in the market were forced to begin to reconsider their intentions of investing in the sector, given the ease with which aviation business activities could be majorly disrupted and brought to a halt. Other issues “Apart from the issues regarding the unions, the AON would also like to draw the attention of the general public to the following clarifications. It is never in the interest of any airline to delay or cancel flights, as this always has severe financial and image consequences. Delays and cancellations are, therefore, the last thing any airline wants. In Nigeria, most of the causes of delays and cancellations are factors that are neither within the control of airlines nor caused by them. “Some of the more prevalent causes of delays and cancellations include, but are by no means limited to, the following: weather, this is the major cause of delays, especially during the rainy seasons and the dust-haze months of November to March. “Inadequate aircraft parking space due to congested aprons in both Lagos and Abuja airports. “Again, because of a deficit in navigational and functional visual aids, as well as inadequate staffing numbers of technical personnel, most of the secondary airports in Nigeria are open between the hours of 7am and 6pm. Once an airline misses this operating window as a result of one or more of the above-mentioned causal factors, airlines are then forced to cancel scheduled flights to such destinations, further compounding the sub-optimal utilisation of their aircraft assets. “VIP movement: The closure of airspace for security reasons to allow certain coded security movements is a significant cause of unpredictable delays across the entire system. This airspace closure for VIP movement, though necessary, has consequences for the operations of airlines. The delays occasioned by this factor are not caused by airlines, yet domestic airlines are regularly held responsible for their impact. “Bird strikes and foreign object damage frequently affect aircraft during taxiing, take-off and landing. The massive delays occasioned by bird strikes are not caused by airlines. “Jet A1 today costs above N2,500 per litre and has continued to rise fast and steadily. On top of the continuous rise in fuel prices, fuel supply is at best epileptic at several secondary airports, thereby causing delays. “Sometimes, airlines have to wait on the ground in a queue for extended periods before being given clearance for take-off. “Inadequate airport infrastructure, including but not limited to poor check-in facilities, lack of adequate screening and exit points, unserviceable baggage carousels, and inadequate and unreliable ground services equipment from ground-handling companies, all cause avoidable systemic delays. “The AON commends the current ongoing construction and rehabilitation activities at the Murtala Muhammed International Airport in Lagos. “While we appreciate the efforts of the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria and the Federal Government to upgrade facilities at the airport terminal and give Nigerians befitting infrastructure, we respectfully request that airlines, who are key stakeholders, be carried along at the early stage to contribute their ideas towards the functionality and flow of the airport facility, so as to address any design flaws that may affect functionality in future.” The post AON condemns airline picketing, warns of investor confidence loss appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: KMA spearheads construction of new Kumasi Central Divisional Police Headquarters, seeks support for relocation
items.description: The Kumasi Metropolitan Assembly (KMA) is spearheading the construction of a new Central Divisional Police Headquarters in the Central Business District (CBD) of Kumasi. The project, estimated at GH¢4.8 million, has been funded by the central government and is expected to replace the existing facility, which has become heavily congested and unsuitable for modern-day policing. Currently, the Ashanti Central Division operates nine offices from the dilapidated structure, with inadequate office space and cells that hamper effective service delivery. According to the Mayor of Kumasi, Kwasi Ofori Agyemang Boadi, the new three-storey facility will provide larger office space, conference rooms, and six modern cells for suspects, including separate detention facilities for juveniles, women, and hardened criminals. He disclosed this when the Ashanti Business Owners Association (ABOA) donated GH¢200,000 to support the relocation of police personnel to pave the way for construction. The project will require the demolition of an old structure within the Ashanti Regional Police Headquarters to make way for the new edifice. Consequently, the Assembly must construct a temporary facility to accommodate the current occupants during the construction period. The temporary structure, which will comprise twelve offices, is estimated to cost GH¢750,000, an amount outside the GH¢4.8 million budget for the main project. To mobilize funds for the temporary facility, the KMA is appealing to corporate institutions and philanthropists for support. So far, GH¢210,000 has been raised, with the latest GH¢200,000 donation from ABOA bringing the total closer to the target. Mr. Ofori Agyemang Boadi is therefore appealing to the public, corporate bodies, and philanthropists to help the Assembly achieve its GH¢750,000 target. Speaking on behalf of ABOA, its Executive Secretary, Charles Kusi Appiah Kubi, said the Association considers the donation as part of its Corporate Social Responsibility to the city in which its members operate. “Safety is the foundation of every development. For businesses, investing in security ensures that we protect our investments,” he said. The Association also pledged to support the Assembly in its efforts to sanitize the Central Business District. Meanwhile, the KMA intends to establish a Metropolitan Police Unit dedicated to the prevention and management of crime within the CBD and believes the completion of the new divisional headquarters will significantly enhance policing in the area.

items.title: Three arrested over alleged kidnapping and murder of 33-year-old phone dealer in Teshie
items.description: The Ghana Police Service has arrested three people in connection with the alleged kidnapping and murder of 33-year-old Nana Yaw Kyere, a phone dealer at the Kwame Nkrumah Circle who was reported missing on September 22. In a press release issued on Monday, September 28, the arrests followed investigations by the Police Missing Persons Unit. The suspects have been identified as Philip Dzifa Kofi Tefe, Sarah Osei Adams and Josiah Obodai. According to a police press release dated September 28, preliminary investigations indicate that Mr Kyere left his residence at Kokomlemle in Accra on September 19 in his Honda Civic but did not return. Police said their investigations established that Mr Kyere was allegedly lured to the residence of suspect Philip Tefe at Teshie Agbleza by Sarah Osei Adams. The police said the two suspects subsequently confessed to their involvement and told investigators that Mr Tefe attacked Mr Kyere during a confrontation, allegedly striking him with a metallic object and causing injuries. The victim was then reportedly moved to another room, where he was left unattended and later died, according to the police account. Investigators further established that Mr Kyere’s body was allegedly transported in a Kia Morning to a location near the motorway on September 20, where it was dumped in a bush and set ablaze. The partially burnt body was discovered at Community 18 on September 21. Police said the victim’s biological mother and an uncle formally identified the remains at the Police Hospital mortuary on 24 September. The police also recovered Mr Kyere’s iPhone 12, which they allege Mr Tefe sold for GH¢100. The alleged buyer, identified as Sunday Omeje, has been cautioned and detained on suspicion of dishonestly receiving the phone. Further investigations led police to arrest Josiah Obodai over his alleged connection with the disposal of the body. Police said a Kia Morning belonging to his father, and believed to have been used to transport the body, has been impounded. The three suspects remain in police custody and are expected to be put before the court as investigations continue. The Ghana Police Service said its investigations are also aimed at identifying and arresting any other people who may have been involved in the case.

items.title: Alan Kyerematen calls for end to political ‘duopoly’ ahead of 2028 election
items.description: United Party (UP) leader Alan John Kwadwo Kyerematen has called on Ghanaians to consider ending the dominance of the two major political parties in the country’s politics ahead of the 2028 general election. Speaking in an interview with Joy Prime’s Nathaniel Attoh, Mr Kyerematen said his long experience in Ghanaian politics and nationwide recognition positioned him to offer voters an alternative to the established political order. “I am an old horse in this game,” he said, adding that in virtually every part of the country, voters either recognise his face or his political brand, Alan Cash. Mr Kyerematen said he believed his political conduct over the years had earned him public goodwill. Mr Kyerematen said his expectation was that voters would make what he described as a “strategic choice” in 2028 to move the country in a different political direction. “My hope is that in 2028, the people of Ghana will make a strategic choice to move our country forward by ending the duopoly,” he said. He attributed what he described as Ghana’s continuing development challenges to the prolonged dominance of the two major political parties, although that remains his political assessment. “It is the duopoly that has created this continuing underdevelopment challenge,” Mr Kyerematen argued. He questioned why, after decades of alternation between the two dominant parties, several basic national challenges remained unresolved. “How is it that two political parties have dominated our politics for 34 years [and] still cannot deal with the challenge of roads?” he asked. Mr Kyerematen cited roads, electricity and access to water among the issues he believes successive administrations have struggled to address. “Our lights don’t stay on,” he said, while also claiming that some Ghanaians had gone decades without running water in their homes. “There are people who have never had water running through their taps for 30 years,” he added. He also raised concerns about Ghana’s education system, particularly recurring difficulties with the computerised school placement process. “Our educational system has so many challenges. Even we can’t work with the computerised system to place students. Every year we have a repeat of these challenges,” he said. The UP leader further pointed to challenges within the health sector, describing them as another indication of the difficulties confronting the country.

items.title: Special delivery: India's Tamil Nadu state hands out gold for newborns
items.description: Authorities in India’s Tamil Nadu state gave babies born in government-run hospitals a free gold ring on Monday, an initiative aimed at boosting confidence in the public healthcare system. Under the scheme launched by actor-turned-Chief Minister Vijay, all babies born in public health facilities in the state are eligible for a one-gramme gold ring, worth some $143. Gold has immense cultural significance in India, featuring prominently in weddings and religious ceremonies, and seen as a safe generational asset. “The gold ring would give the child something valuable to keep for the years ahead,” said one mother at a government hospital in the state’s Madurai district, who declined to give her name. She was among dozens of mothers who cradled their newborns as they queued up to receive the gift. “This scheme feels personal,” another grateful mother, Stella Mary, told AFP. Officials say the initiative aims to highlight maternal and newborn care, while strengthening faith in public healthcare institutions in the southern state of over 72 million people. The scheme, however, drew some criticism from the Bharatiya Janata Party, which is in the opposition in Tamil Nadu. “A gold ring for a newborn may be a welcome gesture, but for families, the most immediate need is ensuring that essential nutrition is available every day,” party member Tamilisai Soundararajan said in a social media post. India’s overcrowded public hospitals often struggle with staff shortages, long waiting times and patchy infrastructure, prompting many patients to seek treatment in the costly private sector. While most women in India give birth in hospitals, home deliveries still occur in some rural communities, making institutional childbirth a priority for health authorities. Despite significant gains in recent years, infant and maternal mortality rates continue to languish in India. The country recorded 24 infant deaths per 1,000 live births while maternal deaths stood at 88 per 100,000 live births, according to latest official data. The gold ring scheme, known as the “Thaimaman” (maternal uncle) programme, draws on the special cultural significance of a child’s maternal uncle, who is often expected to play a key role in family milestones and celebrations. It also taps into India’s enduring obsession with gold. For many women, particularly in rural areas, gold jewellery can serve as a form of personal financial security. India is one of the world’s largest consumers of the metal. According to the World Gold Council, demand in the country reached $25 billion in the first quarter of this year.

items.title: Après une longue absence, Igamane franchit une nouvelle étape vers son retour
items.description: Dans un nouveau signe annonçant son retour prochain sur les terrains, l’international marocain Hamza Igamane a repris le travail avec ballon, en participant à une séance d’entraînement individuelle au centre d’entraînement du club français de Lille, après une longue période d’absence due à une blessure. Le club lillois a publié, au cours des dernières heures, une vidéo sur ses comptes officiels sur les réseaux sociaux, montrant l’attaquant marocain au contact du ballon dans le cadre de son programme de rééducation. Cette séquence témoigne de l’évolution de son état physique, après plusieurs mois consacrés à la récupération de sa pleine condition. Âgé de 23 ans, Igamane poursuit sa rééducation sous la supervision des staffs médical et technique de son club, depuis qu’il a été victime d’une rupture du ligament croisé antérieur du genou droit. Cette blessure l’a éloigné des terrains pendant une longue période et l’a privé de la participation avec la sélection nationale marocaine à la Coupe du monde 2026. Le retour au travail avec ballon constitue ainsi une nouvelle étape dans son processus de rééducation, en attendant la poursuite de son programme progressif et son intégration, en temps voulu, aux entraînements collectifs avant de retrouver la compétition officielle. Les supporters de la sélection marocaine et du LOSC suivent avec attention le retour d’Igamane à sa pleine forme, l’attaquant cherchant à tourner progressivement la page de sa blessure et à retrouver son niveau après cette longue période loin des terrains. items.title: FACEJ SUGU 5 : plus de 16,5 millions de FCFA de chiffre d’affaires
items.description: © Internet La 5ᵉ édition du FACEJ SUGU a permis aux jeunes entrepreneurs maliens de transformer l’exposition de leurs produits et services en opportunités commerciales. Durant les trois jours de l’événement, 103 entreprises ont réalisé un chiffre d’affaires cumulé de 16 559 850 FCFA, soit une moyenne de 160 775 FCFA par entreprise. Les rideaux sont tombés, ce samedi 26 septembre 2026, sur la 5ᵉ édition de la Foire des jeunes entrepreneurs, dénommée FACEJ SUGU. L’événement a réuni 167 entreprises exposantes réparties sur 131 stands, ainsi que des institutions techniques et financières installées sur 19 stands. La fréquentation a également soutenu la dynamique commerciale. Au total, 2 709 visiteurs et clients ont été enregistrés durant les trois jours, soit une moyenne d’un peu plus de 900 visiteurs par jour. Pour la cheffe d’équipe du FACEJ II, Mme Christine Kaboré Kayitesi, ces résultats illustrent l’intérêt d’un espace permettant aux entrepreneurs de présenter directement leurs offres au public. « Le FACEJ SUGU est, pour les jeunes entrepreneurs, une occasion de se retrouver, d’échanger, de développer leur réseau, d’apprendre et surtout de vendre leurs produits et services », a-t-elle souligné. Au-delà des ventes, le FACEJ SUGU a servi de cadre à des échanges sur les difficultés d’accès au financement. Un grand panel a ainsi réuni des institutions financières, des porteurs de projets et des entreprises en activité. L’objectif était de permettre aux entrepreneurs de mieux comprendre les mécanismes de financement, mais aussi d’échanger sur les obstacles qui limitent leur accès aux ressources financières. « Il s’agissait de mieux appréhender le rôle des institutions, mais aussi de comprendre les difficultés liées à l’accès au financement et, ensemble, de trouver des solutions », a expliqué la cheffe d’équipe du FACEJ II. La question du financement a également été abordée sous l’angle de l’entrepreneuriat féminin. Le panel baptisé « Le coin des femmes » a permis de discuter des difficultés rencontrées par les femmes dans leur parcours entrepreneurial et de la nécessité de renforcer leurs réseaux. Nouveau cap Le secrétaire général du ministère de l’Entrepreneuriat national, de l’Emploi et de la Formation professionnelle, M. Drissa Guindo, a exhorté les participants à faire de cette manifestation le point de départ de relations économiques durables. « Je vous invite à maintenir les liens établis au cours de cette édition », a-t-il lancé aux entrepreneurs. Il a également insisté sur la nécessité, pour les entreprises, de renforcer leur compétitivité. « Continuez donc à améliorer la qualité de vos produits et services. Continuez à vous former, continuez à rechercher de nouveaux marchés et de nouveaux partenariats », a-t-il recommandé. Le représentant du ministère a par ailleurs souligné que l’entrepreneuriat ne devait pas rester concentré à Bamako. La participation d’entrepreneurs venus de différentes localités montre, selon lui, l’existence de talents et de savoir-faire à valoriser dans les territoires. La remise d’attestations aux jeunes entrepreneurs, aux écoles partenaires, aux stylistes et aux artisans ayant participé au défilé a donné une dimension symbolique à la clôture de l’événement. Joseph Amara Dembélé

items.title: Un ministre israélien appelle à faire en Cisjordanie «ce que nous avons fait à Gaza»
items.description: Le ministre israelien des Finances Bezalel Smotrich a appele dimanche 27 septembre l'armee a « entrer en guerre » en Cisjordanie occupee et a « y faire ce que nous avons fait a Gaza ». Interroge par Ynet sur les tensions securitaires, le chef du parti Sionisme religieux a aussi reclame le demantelement de l'Autorite palestinienne, qu'il qualifie d'« autorite terroriste ». La reference a Gaza donne a ces propos une portee particulierement lourde. Depuis octobre 2023, l'enclave palestinienne a connu des destructions massives et fait des dizaines de milliers de morts. Appeler a transposer cette methode a la Cisjordanie revient donc a envisager une extension considerable des operations militaires dans un territoire ou vivent trois millions de Palestiniens. Smotrich a parallelement plaide pour l'annexion de territoires a Gaza et dans le sud du Liban. Plus extreme que Bibi Ces declarations reprennent une ligne ancienne. Smotrich defend l'extension de la souverainete israelienne sur la Cisjordanie. En 2024, la Cour internationale de Justice a juge illicite la presence continue d'Israel dans le territoire palestinien occupe et demande l'arret de la colonisation. Israel conteste cette lecture et invoque ses imperatifs de securite. Sur le terrain, la situation s'est fortement deterioree. L'ONU a recense plus de 1 600 attaques de colons ayant fait des victimes ou cause des degâts entre janvier et août 2026, soit 6,7 attaques par jour. Des attaques palestiniennes contre des Israeliens ont aussi eu lieu. Dans ce contexte, les propos de Smotrich ne relevent pas seulement de la provocation : venant d'un ministre influent sur la politique israelienne en Cisjordanie, ils dessinent une orientation susceptible d'aggraver les violences et les deplacements. L'Autorite palestinienne a denonce un appel a la guerre et a l'annexion. a un mois des elections israeliennes , ces propos pesent aussi sur la campagne de Smotrich, figure de l'extreme droite.

items.title: Burkina: «Certains produits» pourraient être «exclusivement importés par l’Etat» contre la surenchère (Président)
items.description: Le président du Faso, le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, répondant à la question sur la hausse des produits de grande consommation, a annoncé que, si les commerçants véreux persistent dans leur comportement répréhensible, «certains produits» pourraient être «exclusivement importés par l'Etat», lors d’un grand oral diffusé dans la nuit du dimanche 27 septembre à la télévision nationale. Lors de son face à face avec la presse, le chef de l’Etat burkinabè, le capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, s’est attardé sur la vie chère. Selon lui, la flambée des prix des produits de première nécessité s’explique par des phénomènes exogènes et endogènes. Malgré les efforts fournis par les structures de contrôle et de répression de l’Etat sur le territoire national, la situation persiste. «Il y a des prix qui peuvent flamber sans notre volonté. Sur le plan international, vous allez trouver certaines matières où le prix va flamber», a dit le capitaine Traoré, évoquant le cas du carburant dont le gasoil a subi une hausse de 75 F sur le litre. Selon lui, cette augmentation est à leur corps défendant, enchaînant que «le plus important, c'est à l'intérieur, c'est nous-mêmes». «Il y a des réactionnaires qui ont un agenda avec les impérialistes, qui font tout pour faire disparaître des produits pour faire la spéculation, qui sabotent, qui font monter les prix. Ils s'entendent et le font pour juste amener la population à rejeter la révolution. C'est leur seul objectif pour certains», a-t-il souligné. Le chef de l'Etat burkinabè, le capitaine Ibrahim Traoré Le chef de l’Etat a salué les structures de contrôle qui «font des efforts, ferment certaines boutiques». «C'est bien. Mais nous avons toujours dit aux commerçants véreux de faire attention et d'arrêter parce que l'Etat est en mesure de tout faire. Et s'ils n'arrêtent pas, le jour où l'Etat prend cette décision, ce sera irréversible». Il a insisté qu’après la création de Faso Yaar, si aujourd'hui les commerçants véreux persistent dans leur comportement, l’Etat va passer à une nouvelle dimension. «Et bientôt, certains produits, nous pourrons dire que ce sera exclusivement importé par l'État. Et là, Faso Yaar imposera le prix», a lancé le capitaine Ibrahim Traoré. Le président du Faso, le capitaine Ibrahim Traoré a ajouté que l’Etat «est en mesure de recruter des jeunes gens, les former, les installer et leurs donner le produit en avance avec le prix fixé partout sur le territoire, ils vont vendre. Et ceux (commerçants) qui sont dans ça (mauvais comportement), ils vont fermer boutique. Donc, on a dit aux gens de faire attention. Si on décide, on va le faire». Par Wakat Séra L’article Burkina: «Certains produits» pourraient être «exclusivement importés par l'Etat» contre la surenchère (Président) est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Lahore ATC extends physical remand of PTI's Hammad Azhar for 7 days in Jinnah House attack case
items.description: LAHORE: An anti-terrorism court (ATC) on Monday extended the physical remand of PTI leader Hammad Azhar for another seven days in the 2023 Jinnah House attack case . Sarwar Road police had booked several PTI leaders and workers on charges of attacking and vandalising the Jinnah House , which also serves as the residence of the corps commander, during the May 9, 2023 protests against the arrest of ex-premier Imran Khan. On Monday, police produced the former federal finance minister before ATC Judge Manzer Ali Gill upon the completion of his 21-day physical remand . During the hearing, a state prosecutor said police needed further remand to recover the suspect’s mobile phone and SIM, describing them as important pieces of evidence. He urged the court to extend the remand for a further seven days. Speaking before the court, Azhar questioned why further remand was being sought, saying he had already been kept on physical remand for 21 days in an alleged occurrence where he said he was not even present. “Even a murder suspect is sent on 14-day remand here. Has my offence become more serious than murder?” he asked. The former minister also complained that he had earlier not been allowed to meet his lawyers or family members — a concern also voiced earlier by his family before a court. The ATC then reserved its decision on the prosecution’s request for further remand, and later announced its decision, granting the police Azhar’s remand for another seven days. Meeting with family allowed, LHC told Separately, a two-member Lahore High Court (LHC) bench headed by Justice Syed Shahbaz Ali Rizvi disposed of a petition filed by Azhar’s mother and wife against the alleged denial of access to him during police custody. A Lahore ATC had already disposed of a similar plea filed by the family, directing them to approach the police on the matter. A Punjab government lawyer informed the LHC bench that Azhar had been allowed to meet his mother and wife. The law officer further said that the PTI leader would also meet his lawyer at the trial court on Monday. Relying on the government lawyer’s statement, the bench disposed of the petition. According to his family , Azhar was arrested on Sept 5. However, police said the next day they were unaware of his arrest, prompting the PTI leader’s mother to approach the LHC on Sept 7, and he was produced before an ATC the same day. Azhar, the son of late former Punjab governor Mian Muhammad Azhar , has been declared a proclaimed offender by multiple anti-terrorism courts for not joining the proceedings against him in cases related to the May 9 riots . Azhar had reappeared in public on May 22, 2024, a year after he had gone into hiding when the state launched a crackdown against the party leadership following the violent incidents of May 9 . At the time, the PTI leader had evaded arrest when the Counter-Terrorism Department raided the party’s secretariat in Islamabad.

items.title: Feijóo, ante la plana mayor del PP: “Nadie va a resolver el problema de la vivienda en cinco minutos”
items.description: El Partido Popular quiere mantener el foco en Ceuta por encima de la crisis de la vivienda, como se ha percibido en el discurso de Alberto Núñez Feijóo este lunes ante la Junta Directiva Nacional del PP, el máximo órgano entre congresos de los populares. El líder del PP ha dedicado toda la primera parte de su intervención ante la plana mayor del PP a los problemas que persisten dos meses después en la ciudad autónoma, y ha anunciado que su partido pondrá en marcha una nueva comisión de investigación en el Senado sobre la entrada masiva de finales de julio. Solo después de una larga exposición sobre Ceuta, Feijóo ha entrado en harina sobre la crisis de la vivienda, en el centro de la actualidad desde el desalojo de la anciana Maricarmen, hasta el punto de que ha motivado una nueva acampada en la Puerta del Sol de Madrid que reclama medidas urgentes para intervenir en el mercado. El líder del PP ha acusado al Gobierno de Pedro Sánchez de haber “fracasado” en esta materia, pero de alguna manera también ha admitido que, si gobierna, tampoco el PP tendrá fácil atajarlo. “Nadie va a resolver el problema de la vivienda en cinco minutos”, ha admitido Feijóo. Tunisie | Feuille de route de l’Ordre des ingénieurs pour la sécurité énergétique
items.description: Pour renforcer la sécurité énergétique en Tunisie et mettre fin aux problèmes survenus durant l’été 2026, avec les coupures intempestives d’électricité, l’Ordre des ingénieurs tunisiens a élaboré une «feuille de route énergétique», a indiqué le doyen des ingénieurs, Mohsen Gharsi, dans une publication sur le réseaux sociaux. Dans ladite feuille de route, l’Ordre des ingénieurs ne s’est pas limité à un simple diagnostic de la situation ou à des considérations générales sur le secteur, mais a mobilisé des compétences en ingénierie et des expertises pointues pour présenter des propositions pratiques dans le domaine de l’énergie. La problématique ne réside pas uniquement à augmenter la capacité électrique installée, mais dans la capacité réelle du système à répondre à la demande lors des pics de consommation, notamment en période de fortes chaleurs, a souligné Gharsi, en rappelant la nécessité d’une approche intégrée, englobant l’approvisionnement en gaz, la production électrique, la maintenance des réseaux, le développement des énergies renouvelables, le stockage de l'électricité, ainsi que la maîtrise de la demande, le financement des nouveaux projets et la gouvernance du système. La feuille de route propose plusieurs pistes opérationnelles, telles que le rétablissement de la capacité disponible grâce à des opérations de maintenance, la sécurisation de l’approvisionnement lors des pics de demande, le développement de l’autoproduction d’électricité à partir de l’énergie solaire, la protection des infrastructures critiques ainsi que le développement des systèmes de stockage. Le doyen des ingénieurs a également insisté sur la nécessité d’entamer dès maintenant les préparatifs pour l’été 2027, compte tenu du temps limité dont on dispose pour prendre des décisions et mener à bien les opérations de maintenance, la mobilisation des investissements et la mise en route des solutions envisagées. Il faut absolument éviter que ne se reproduisent, l’été prochain, les difficultés rencontrées par le pays durant l’été 2026, a-t-il insisté M. Gharsi a précisé que l’Ordre des ingénieurs ne cherche pas à se substituer à l’État, au gouvernement ou à la Société tunisienne de l’électricité et du gaz (Steg), mais qu’il met son expertise et ses compétences en ingénierie à la disposition de l’État afin de l’aider à relever les défis auxquels est confronté le secteur de l'énergie. L’objectif maintenant est de passer de la phase d’étude et de recherche des solutions à celle de la mise en œuvre des propositions et de la concrétisation des décisions, programmes et projets. Par ailleurs, M. Gharsi a salué les efforts des ingénieurs et experts ayant contribué à l’élaboration de cette feuille de route, affirmant que le rôle de l’ingénieur ne se limite pas au diagnostic des problèmes, mais englobe également la proposition de solutions et la participation à leur mise en œuvre. Il a conclu en affirmant la disposition de l’Ordre des ingénieurs à poursuivre le débat sur la feuille de route, à en enrichir les propositions et à contribuer à leur mise en œuvre, considérant que la sécurité énergétique ne relève plus de la seule dimension technique, mais qu’elle est également liée à la souveraineté économique, à la stabilité sociale et aux droits des générations futures. I. B. L’article Tunisie | Feuille de route de l’Ordre des ingénieurs pour la sécurité énergétique est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: Supply Ministry postpones bread price review amid ongoing push from bakeries, mills
items.description: Supply Minister Sherif Farouk has asked for a week’s review period before the ministry responds to a request to raise its guideline consumer prices for two categories of non-subsidized bread, according to a source who was present at a Sunday meeting where representatives from bakeries and mills put forward their request. The request is their second in just a few months, following a dispute over the extent of the ministry’s role in setting and enforcing non-subsidized bread prices. Their push for higher guideline prices comes as the industry’s production costs rise steadily, with wheat prices spiralling again amid an escalation in the intensity of Russia’s war on Ukraine, and as domestic fuel prices continue to rise against the backdrop of the regional war. Farouk said the ministry would review price movements over the coming week, and, if prices did not fall over that period, the ministry would revise guideline prices for the tourist and fino bread categories, the source said. The ministry did not commit to a specific percentage increase. Senior representatives of the General Bakeries Division raised the issue of production costs at the meeting and called for a review of tourist and fino bread prices, proposing a 15 percent increase. Milling sector representatives also presented an update on the wheat and flour markets and recent pressures on production costs, particularly higher maritime shipping and logistics costs and rising global wheat prices amid the shipping disruptions in the Black Sea. Imported wheat reached record prices at the beginning of this week, rising to between LE16,600 and LE16,800 for Ukrainian wheat and LE17,000 for Russian wheat, compared with a maximum of LE12,200 to LE12,500 per ton in June. Bakeries selling tourist bread rely on the free market for their flour supplies, which account for more than 50 percent of production costs, the source said. Transport and other operating costs have also risen, leaving bakeries facing significant losses. The meeting is the latest in a series of calls bakeries have made to the ministry regarding tourist and fino bread prices, which intensified in August as flour and other production costs increased. The Supply Ministry did not respond to the demands, issuing a directive instead on August 4 to maintain the prices and weights for tourist and fino bread set in March . As bakeries continued to call for price increases, sources in the sector questioned the legal basis for the imposition of mandatory pricing on tourist bread, whose production inputs are not subsidized. Lawyer Khaled Ali previously told Mada Masr however that since wheat is a “strategic commodity,” the ministry has a role in market oversight. The ministry also threatened legal action against violators of its price directives at the time, with Interior Ministry statements later announcing “large scale campaigns to control supply crimes” against those violating Supply Ministry decisions on prices and weights. The changes in wheat and flour prices come amid volatility in global wheat markets, particularly continued tensions in the Black Sea region, the main source of Egypt’s wheat imports. Import data for the first eight months of the year showed that Russia and Ukraine together accounted for more than 82 percent of Egypt’s wheat imports, despite repeated announcements by the Supply Ministry of plans to diversify import origins. The post Supply Ministry postpones bread price review amid ongoing push from bakeries, mills first appeared on Mada Masr .
